blocks.content: This closing topic covers resource exhaustion at a broader scale than any single Pod, a node, or an entire cluster genuinely running out of usable capacity, and the real fixes and prevention covered elsewhere in this course.

Where OOMKilled, covered earlier in this module, is about one specific container exceeding its own limit, resource exhaustion describes a node, or the whole cluster, genuinely running low on usable capacity across everything running on it.

blocks.alt: A node or cluster-wide capacity problem, not one isolated container

blocks.content: This connects directly back to the Failed Scheduling topic covered earlier in this module, if the cluster genuinely has no free capacity anywhere, new Pods simply cannot be placed, and pile up in Pending.

blocks.alt: The exact Failed Scheduling symptom covered earlier, now understood as a cluster-wide capacity signal

blocks.content: Under genuine node-level pressure, kubelet can actively evict already-running Pods to reclaim resources, a more severe symptom than simply failing to schedule new ones, existing, working Pods are actually removed.

blocks.alt: A more severe symptom, already-running Pods actively removed, not just new ones blocked

blocks.content: Exactly the Cluster Autoscaler covered in the Autoscaling module, adding genuine, additional node capacity automatically is the real, structural fix for recurring resource exhaustion, not a one-time manual intervention.

blocks.alt: The exact automated mechanism covered in the Autoscaling module, adding real capacity

blocks.content: This is where ResourceQuota and LimitRange, both covered in the Namespaces & Resource Management module, genuinely earn their keep, keeping any single namespace or Pod from consuming far more than its fair share in the first place, preventing exhaustion before it happens, not just reacting to it.

blocks.alt: Proactive prevention, covered in its own dedicated module, stopping the problem before it starts

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Resource exhaustion is a node or cluster-wide capacity problem, showing up as new Pods stuck Pending or, more severely, existing Pods actively evicted.
The Cluster Autoscaler is the real structural fix, adding genuine capacity, while ResourceQuota and LimitRange are the proactive prevention that stops it from happening in the first place.
